properties.name: 9 of the 14 interfaces counting toward seam coverage have an EMPTY spec — the number measures declaration, not contract
properties.statement:
ASKED 2026-09-10, after a session asserted without measuring that declaring six Interface nodes would move the seams band "68% -> 100% either way". The "either way" half is CONFIRMED and is worse than the claim: most existing coverage is already content-free.

MEASURED, three ways:

① CODE. `seam_sets_at` (maturity.rs) scans Interface nodes, walks incoming PROVIDES and CONSUMES, and inserts the component pair into `declared`. There is NO reference to `spec` anywhere in that path — no emptiness test, no content test. A boundary is "covered" when an Interface node exists with a provider and a consumer attached.

② DATA. Of 22 Interfaces, 14 have both ends attached and therefore count toward coverage. NINE OF THOSE FOURTEEN HAVE A COMPLETELY EMPTY SPEC:
  ifc:graph-read (16 consumers), ifc:ingress-trust-boundary, ifc:kv-backend,
  ifc:llm-backend, ifc:provenance-sidecar, ifc:reasoning-channel,
  ifc:rendezvous-sidecar, ifc:session-graph-selector, ifc:temporal-api
`ifc:graph-read` is the most-consumed boundary in the design and says nothing at all.

③ SCOPE. `detect_incomplete_published_contracts` filters to `published`/`both`. All ten `internal` interfaces — including all nine empties above — are skipped.

⭐ THE CLASS, WHICH IS NOT "seam_coverage IS WRONG". Two instruments each measure half the question and their scopes do not meet. One asks DOES A CONTRACT EXIST (any designation, content never read); the other asks DOES IT SAY ANYTHING (content read, published only). An `internal` interface with an empty spec is counted as coverage by the first and invisible to the second. Nothing in the design can tell "this boundary has a real contract" from "somebody made a node".

⭐ AND IT HAS RECURRED. `dec:idea-what-would-a-provided-contract-buy-substitution-derived-tests-or-a-mock` recorded on 2026-08-21 that `internal` interfaces were 0 of 4 with a substantive spec, and that two of the four `published` "specs" were provenance correction notes naming "no operation, no input and no output". A PERSON found that by hand and wrote it into a decision. No detector reported it then and none reports it now — which is the test for cause versus trigger: fixing the class would have caught the earlier occurrence too.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED, and the original claim is only half verified. Whether declaring six more interfaces reaches exactly 100% is STILL UNMEASURED — nobody has run it, and any 100% at subsystem altitude is bounded by the 7 coupling/contract pairs that `seam_coverage` reports it DROPPED because an endpoint reached no container at that level. Also unmeasured: whether the published-scoped completeness detector actually rejects the two provenance-note specs, which are non-empty strings and may pass a length-shaped test. Content-length is not content, and that is the same class one level deeper.
